texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1. Purpose and Objectives
texts.text: 1. Purpose and Objectives

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Nexora  Technologies  Ltd.  ("Nexora"  or  "the  Company")  expects  its  people  to  travel  and  incur business expenses when this helps serve customers, deliver projects and build the business. This policy sets out what the Company will pay for, how much it will pay, how employees must claim, and how Finance reviews and settles those claims.
texts.text: Nexora  Technologies  Ltd.  ("Nexora"  or  "the  Company")  expects  its  people  to  travel  and  incur business expenses when this helps serve customers, deliver projects and build the business. This policy sets out what the Company will pay for, how much it will pay, how employees must claim, and how Finance reviews and settles those claims.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The policy has four objectives. First, it protects employees from paying out of pocket for legitimate business  costs.  Second,  it  gives  managers  and  Finance  one  consistent  standard,  so  that  two employees of the same grade travelling to the same city are treated the same way. Third, it keeps the Company compliant with the Income Tax Act, the GST law and its own audit requirements. Fourth, it keeps travel spending proportionate to the value of the work being done.
texts.text: The policy has four objectives. First, it protects employees from paying out of pocket for legitimate business  costs.  Second,  it  gives  managers  and  Finance  one  consistent  standard,  so  that  two employees of the same grade travelling to the same city are treated the same way. Third, it keeps the Company compliant with the Income Tax Act, the GST law and its own audit requirements. Fourth, it keeps travel spending proportionate to the value of the work being done.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This policy works together with two companion documents. The Meal and Hotel Spending Limits document (NX-FIN-POL-013) holds the detailed limits by grade and city tier. The Approval Rules and  Exceptions document  (NX-FIN-POL-014)  holds  the  approval  matrix  and  the  exception catalogue  (codes  EX-01  to  EX-12).  Where  this  policy  refers  to  a  limit  or  an  exception  code,  the companion document is the authority.

Contractors are covered only to the extent that their contract provides for reimbursement of expenses.

texts.orig: 5.1 General principle
texts.text: 5.1 General principle

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Employees must choose the most economical option that is reasonable for the purpose of the trip, taking  into  account  time,  safety  and  the  cost  of  lost  working  hours.  The  cheapest  fare  is  not mandatory  when  a  slightly  dearer  option  saves  a  night  in  a  hotel  or  avoids  a  missed  customer meeting, but the reason must be stated in the claim.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Domestic flights are booked in economy class for all grades. The cap for a domestic return fare is INR 22,000.
texts.text: Domestic flights are booked in economy class for all grades. The cap for a domestic return fare is INR 22,000.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · International flights are booked in economy class up to INR 80,000 for return travel. Vice presidents (L6) may book business class on flights longer than six hours, up to INR 160,000.
texts.text: International flights are booked in economy class up to INR 80,000 for return travel. Vice presidents (L6) may book business class on flights longer than six hours, up to INR 160,000.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Directors (L5) may book premium economy on flights longer than six hours, where available.
texts.text: Directors (L5) may book premium economy on flights longer than six hours, where available.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Domestic tickets must be booked at least 7 days before departure and international tickets at least 14 days before. Shorter notice requires exception EX-04 or EX-11.
texts.text: Domestic tickets must be booked at least 7 days before departure and international tickets at least 14 days before. Shorter notice requires exception EX-04 or EX-11.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.3 Rail travel
texts.text: 5.3 Rail travel

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Employees in grades L1 and L2 travel by 3AC, and employees in grades L3 and above by 2AC, on routes where the journey is under 12 hours. Tatkal charges are reimbursed only when the travel could not be planned earlier. Where a train is available at a reasonable time, the manager may ask the employee to prefer rail over air for journeys under 500 kilometres.
texts.text: Employees in grades L1 and L2 travel by 3AC, and employees in grades L3 and above by 2AC, on routes where the journey is under 12 hours. Tatkal charges are reimbursed only when the travel could not be planned earlier. Where a train is available at a reasonable time, the manager may ask the employee to prefer rail over air for journeys under 500 kilometres.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.4 Local transport
texts.text: 5.4 Local transport

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Local cabs, autorickshaws, metro and bus fares for business movement in the destination city are reimbursed  up  to  INR  1,500  per  day  of  the  trip.  Airport  transfers  are  included  in  the  daily  cap. Employees are  encouraged  to  use  app-based  cabs  so  that  a  trip  record  exists.  Late-night  travel, defined as a ride that starts between 10 pm and 6 am, may exceed the cap under exception EX-09, since safety is more important than cost.

texts.orig: 5.5 Own vehicle
texts.text: 5.5 Own vehicle

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When an employee uses a personal  vehicle  for  business  travel  with  prior  manager  approval,  the Company reimburses INR 12 per kilometre for a car and INR 5 per kilometre for a two-wheeler. This rate covers fuel, wear and maintenance. Toll and parking charges are reimbursed separately against receipts. Distance is taken from a mapping application screenshot attached to the claim.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Claims are raised in the Expense Portal. A complete claim contains one entry per trip, the stated purpose of the trip, one line per expense with the correct category, and a scanned or photographed receipt for each line above the exemption threshold.
texts.text: Claims are raised in the Expense Portal. A complete claim contains one entry per trip, the stated purpose of the trip, one line per expense with the correct category, and a scanned or photographed receipt for each line above the exemption threshold.

texts.label: text

A claim submitted more than 60 days after the trip end date will be rejected unless the CFO approves it.  Claims  will  not  be  accepted  after  90  days  under  any  circumstances,  except  where  a documented medical or legal reason prevented submission.

texts.orig: 9. Travel Advances and Settlement

texts.label: text
texts.orig: An employee who expects to spend more than INR 20,000 on a trip may request an advance of up to 50 percent of the estimated cost. The request must be raised at least 5 working days before travel, with an itinerary and an estimate. Advances for international travel may be raised up to 70 percent of the estimate, given the higher forex and visa costs.

texts.label: text

Any unspent balance is returned to the Company through bank transfer, or recovered from salary after notice  if  it  remains  unsettled  for  30  days.  A  new  advance  is  not  issued  while  an  earlier  one  is outstanding.

texts.orig: 12. Taxes, GST and Forex
texts.text: 12. Taxes, GST and Forex

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Hotel tariffs attract GST of 12 percent for rooms priced between INR 1,000 and INR 7,500 per night and  18  percent  above  that.  Input  tax  credit  can  be  claimed  only  when  the  invoice  carries  the Company's GSTIN, so employees must give the Company's registration details at check-in. Airline tickets in economy class attract 5 percent GST and in business class 12 percent; the GST invoice must be attached.

Input  tax  credit  can  be  claimed  only  when  the  invoice  carries  the Company's GSTIN, so employees must give the Company's registration details at check-in. Airline tickets in economy class attract 5 percent GST and in business class 12 percent; the GST invoice must be attached.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Where an invoice is issued without the Company GSTIN, the claim is still reimbursed, but Finance records the tax as a cost. Repeated omission by the same employee is reported to the manager. Foreign currency amounts are converted at the card statement rate; any forex markup charged by the bank is reimbursed in full for business spend.

texts.orig: 14. Audit, Compliance and Consequences
texts.text: 14. Audit, Compliance and Consequences

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Internal Audit selects a sample of claims every quarter, with a focus on high-value claims, claims with exceptions and claims from employees with repeated exceptions. Finance runs automated checks for duplicate receipts, weekend spending patterns and amounts just below approval thresholds.
texts.text: Internal Audit selects a sample of claims every quarter, with a focus on high-value claims, claims with exceptions and claims from employees with repeated exceptions. Finance runs automated checks for duplicate receipts, weekend spending patterns and amounts just below approval thresholds.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Breaches are handled in proportion to what happened. An honest mistake leads to correction and, where  needed,  recovery  of  the  amount.  Repeated  carelessness  leads  to  a  written  warning  and temporary  withdrawal  of  the  right  to  claim  without  pre-approval.  Deliberate  false  claims,  altered receipts  or  collusion  are  treated  as  misconduct  and  lead  to  disciplinary  action  up  to  termination, recovery of the amount and, where the law requires, reporting to authorities.

texts.orig: 15. Frequently Asked Questions
texts.text: 15. Frequently Asked Questions

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: My flight was INR 25,000 return and the cap is INR 22,000. What happens?
texts.text: Q: My flight was INR 25,000 return and the cap is INR 22,000. What happens?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: The extra amount is above the cap. You can ask for exception EX-04 if the booking was urgent, otherwise the excess is not reimbursed.
texts.text: A: The extra amount is above the cap. You can ask for exception EX-04 if the booking was urgent, otherwise the excess is not reimbursed.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Can I claim a meal if the customer paid for lunch?
texts.text: Q: Can I claim a meal if the customer paid for lunch?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: No. You may claim only for the meals you paid for yourself.
texts.text: A: No. You may claim only for the meals you paid for yourself.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: I lost my hotel bill. Can I still claim?
texts.text: Q: I lost my hotel bill. Can I still claim?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: Ask the hotel for a duplicate invoice. If this is not possible, use a lost-receipt declaration (EX-05), which is allowed up to INR 2,000 per claim.
texts.text: A: Ask the hotel for a duplicate invoice. If this is not possible, use a lost-receipt declaration (EX-05), which is allowed up to INR 2,000 per claim.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: How long do I have to submit a claim?
texts.text: Q: How long do I have to submit a claim?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: 30 days from the trip end date. Up to 60 days with exception EX-06; after that only the CFO can approve it.
texts.text: A: 30 days from the trip end date. Up to 60 days with exception EX-06; after that only the CFO can approve it.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Can I upgrade my room using my own money?
texts.text: Q: Can I upgrade my room using my own money?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: Yes, you can pay the difference yourself. Claim only the entitled amount, and attach the invoice.
texts.text: A: Yes, you can pay the difference yourself. Claim only the entitled amount, and attach the invoice.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Do I get a daily allowance for travelling?
texts.text: Q: Do I get a daily allowance for travelling?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: No. Meals are paid on actuals up to the limit.
texts.text: A: No. Meals are paid on actuals up to the limit.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: I travelled with a colleague. Who claims the shared cab?
texts.text: Q: I travelled with a colleague. Who claims the shared cab?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: The senior employee claims it and lists the colleague's name in the description.
texts.text: A: The senior employee claims it and lists the colleague's name in the description.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Can I claim an Uber to the airport at midnight above the daily cap?
texts.text: Q: Can I claim an Uber to the airport at midnight above the daily cap?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: Yes, if you raise exception EX-09 for late-night safety.
texts.text: A: Yes, if you raise exception EX-09 for late-night safety.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Who approves my claim if my manager is on leave?
texts.text: Q: Who approves my claim if my manager is on leave?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A: The delegate named in the portal, or the department head if no delegate is set.
texts.text: A: The delegate named in the portal, or the department head if no delegate is set.

texts.orig: Q: My claim was returned. What now?
texts.text: Q: My claim was returned. What now?

texts.text: A: Fix the missing item and resubmit within 15 days to keep the original date.
